So a segment with distinct endpoints is not tree-like, and a tree-like path has zero increment, as its trivial signature requires at the first level.

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a vector in a real normed space and $T \ge 0$. The path $t \mapsto \min(t, T - t)\, x$ on $[0, T]$ runs linearly from $0$ to $\tfrac{T}{2} x$ and back to $0$. It is tree-like, with height function $h(t) = \min(t, T - t)\, \|x\|$: the increment between two times is at most the difference of their heights.
nodes.title: A segment traversed out and back is tree-like
